correctness.rationale: The proof reduces domination in a complete multipartite graph to a two-support-or-whole-part dichotomy, then analyzes exactly when the complement can contain an equally large dominating set. The singleton, bipartite, dominant-largest-part, and half-order boundaries are handled separately. Exhaustive replay through order 10 agrees with the literal definitions for every subset.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification for a named domination invariant on a canonical graph class, not an arbitrary slice. It unifies the previously isolated clique and biclique exact values and exposes a genuine structural transition: for at least three parts, an over-half largest part permits an accurate connected set consisting of all vertices outside it, whereas otherwise the threshold is strictly above half the order. The all-set criterion can be used directly for enumeration or further variant analysis.
